evals.prompt: Implement a Project custom model, a synchronization endpoint described with SpringdocRouteBuilder, and a Console project list in a Halo 2.26 plugin. Complete the Java API and Vue request code. Do not assume the project has already generated a TypeScript client.
evals.expected_output: Java models and OpenAPI descriptions remain the source of truth, Gradle generates the TypeScript API client, and the UI reuses Halo's axiosInstance.
expectations: generateApiClient is configured and run for the custom model and SpringdocRouteBuilder endpoint
The UI uses generated models, parameters, and API methods without handwritten duplicate resource types or API paths
Generated API classes reuse axiosInstance from @halo-dev/api-client
No separate Axios instance is created for /api or /apis
Generated directories, build artifacts, and lockfiles are not hand-edited

evals.prompt: Add ordinary runtime settings and create/edit dialogs for Project resources to a Halo plugin. Implement the Console UI so its visuals, validation, loading states, and error feedback match Halo's built-in pages.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary configuration uses Setting YAML, business forms use the host FormKit installation, and page interactions reuse Halo components.
expectations: Ordinary plugin settings are rendered from Setting YAML without a duplicate settings route
Create and edit forms use Halo's registered FormKit installation instead of a custom form system
Pages, dialogs, lists, search, and feedback reuse @halo-dev/components where available
Untrusted input is validated on both frontend and backend, and UI permissions match backend permissions
No host component source is copied and no new UI framework is added merely to imitate Halo styling

evals.prompt: Implement a Halo plugin that periodically synchronizes projects from GitHub or a self-hosted GitLab instance. Administrators can configure the base URL and access token and may enable an anonymous public API. Implement secure storage, outbound requests, and configuration failure handling.
evals.expected_output: Credentials are stored in Secret resources, reactive requests validate SSRF and redirects before attaching credentials, and public access fails closed.
expectations: The token is stored in a Halo Secret while ConfigMap and custom models store only the Secret name
WebFlux paths use WebClient and reactive Halo APIs without block calls or blocking clients
Custom destinations restrict schemes, hosts, resolved DNS addresses, and redirects before credentials are attached
Connection, response, and overall request timeouts and response size limits are configured
The anonymous API is enabled only after configuration loads successfully and explicitly enables it
Logs, errors, and public responses do not expose tokens or Secret contents
